artifacts.summary: Audits the web->typescript dependency wiring: confirms the manifest dependency is mechanically safe (no cycle, depth 2 of 5), finds the two web agents load context via a static per-agent @-reference list (not index.json load_when) so the manifest edit alone does not auto-load typescript context, identifies the exact two duplicate subsections (43 lines) in typescript-web.md to trim, and recommends the concrete fix.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent system, a declared extension `dependencies` array (manifest.json) only guarantees the dependency's files are deployed -- it does NOT make a dependent extension's agents actually read the dependency's context tree. web-research-agent.md/web-implementation-agent.md (and, by the same mechanism, any other extension's agents) discover context via a static, hand-authored per-agent `## Context References` @-pointer list, not a dynamic index.json load_when query at dispatch time (grep for load_when/jq/index.json in either file returns zero matches). To make a new dependency functionally load context for the dependent's agents, add one @-reference line to each consuming agent's Context References section pointing at the dependency's own context-tree README (mirroring typescript-research-agent.md's own one-line-to-its-README pattern), and rely on that README's Loading Strategy table for on-demand discovery of the rest -- do not expect index-entries.json load_when edits alone to have any effect on these two agents.

The extension loader (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/init.lua) enforces a recursion depth limit of 5 and circular-dependency detection via a loading stack during manifest `dependencies` resolution; an already-loaded dependency is skipped (not reloaded), and a dependency load failure aborts the parent extension's load before copying any files. Unloading an extension another loaded extension depends on is a hard block (`ERROR: Cannot unload 'X' -- required by: Y`), refused before any confirmation dialog.
